- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 2–5%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by overcorrection, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and shift mean reversion downward.
- If model forecast mean is significantly higher than recent 18-day average, apply downward bias correction (−1.5 to −3.0%).
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from neutral to positive, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0σ above recent mean.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift downward; adjust forecast to align with recent 18-day mean.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extrapolating from 18-day trend; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility amplification.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 5–7 days after spike, model overreacts; reduce forecast slope after spike by 30–50%.
